answers.answer: Rule a clearing by comparing each player's warriors plus buildings; tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop another player ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: rule determined by total warriors plus buildings; tokens/pawns excluded; ordinary ties and Eyrie/Vagabond exceptions stated.

answers.answer: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from a clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing, and rule the origin or destination or both. Recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple moves during one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions → Move (4.2).

answers.answer: Defender may play one matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise defender immediately deals two hits, regardless of its warrior count, and battle ends if attacker has no warriors or pawns left. Resolve before-roll effects, roll, and after-roll effects. Higher die is attacker hits and lower is defender hits (equal dice equal results); rolled hits cap at each side's warriors in battle, with Alliance defense reversing dice and Vagabond using undamaged swords instead. Add extra hits (uncapped), subtract ignored hits; if defender has no warriors, attacker deals one defenseless extra hit (Vagabond instead is defenseless with no undamaged swords). Each hit removes an opposing piece; hit recipient chooses removal order but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens. Both sides deal counted hits; later warrior losses do not change roll cap. A player removing an enemy building/token scores one VP each, even defending or outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
answers.evidence: Actions → Battle (4.3), six-step order and removal/scoring rules.

answers.answer: Craft by activating crafting pieces matching the crafting icons at the bottom left of the card, not by paying the card's suit. Each crafting piece activates once per turn; Vagabond can reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted unless that item is in the map supply. Persistent effects cannot be duplicated if an identical persistent effect is already in your play area; the existing card stays out of hand and cannot be spent or discarded unless instructed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Craft (4.1): icons, once-per-turn limit and Vagabond exception, supply requirement, persistent-effect duplicate rule.

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from your hand, put it in your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. Win at the start of your own Birdsong by ruling three clearings of the matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit, or (bird dominance) two diagonally opposite corner clearings. An activated dominance card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. Bird dominance remains bird, so taking it requires a bird card; a bird card may pay for a non-bird dominance card. Taking and activating it are separate and do not use a faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: For two players remove all four dominance cards before shuffling; each player draws three cards. Cover the four R slots with ruins. Map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. Keep R-marked ruin items separate: only Vagabond setup hides one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, one per ruin; with no Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Setup factions in order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond (distinct from turn order). The summary also provides each faction's Standard Setup, including Marquise keep/warriors/buildings, Eyrie roost/warriors/leader, Alliance bases/sympathy/supporters, and Vagabond character/pawn/quests/items/relationships.
answers.evidence: Setup: two-player rule, ruins and items, faction setup order, and four faction setup subsections.

answers.answer: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep's clearing; other players may move pieces into it. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed. Whenever Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this works outside battle too. Without the Keep there is no destination for Field Hospitals, so it cannot be rebuilt after removal.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts with crafting using workshops, then up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order. March is one compound action of up to two moves and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is limited to once per turn; if supply is insufficient, place the maximum available. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Daylight action list.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type and pay the cost at the top of its column by removing wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place it and score VP shown on the uncovered track space. You need the full wood cost, building, and legal slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Build action.

answers.answer: Birdsong: (1) Emergency Orders: if hand is empty, draw one. (2) Add one or two cards from hand to the Decree, at most one bird card, in any columns. (3) If there are no roosts on map, place a roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all these pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Birdsong steps.

answers.answer: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card column by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column choose card order freely and birds are wild. Recruit places one warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic). Move at least one warrior from a matching clearing subject to normal movement rules. Battle in a matching clearing with your warriors and an enemy. Build a roost in a matching clearing you rule with an open slot and no existing roost. If any required action cannot be fully completed, Turmoil starts immediately; cannot skip that card or continue other columns.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight, Decree action requirements and Turmoil trigger.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up first); then retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends and proceed to Evening. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings. Evening still scores the rightmost empty roost-track space, draws, and discards to five.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Turmoil, in order; Evening, even after turmoil.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting, to Supporters; a group move costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. The supporter capacity still applies: with no bases it is five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded; with a base there is no cap. Battle alone and moving only the Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Outrage and Supporters.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, resolve any number of Revolts first, then any number of Spread Sympathy actions. Revolt: choose a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on your board; spend two matching supporters; remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP per enemy building/token removed, place the matching base, and place warriors equal to matching-suit sympathy count plus one in Officers. Vagabond instead damages three items. Spread Sympathy: choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy (or any clearing if no sympathy exists), pay the matching supporter cost shown by next token; Martial Law adds one matching supporter if one other player has at least three warriors there. Place one sympathy token and score its uncovered VP. Keep's placement ban applies. Summary distinguishes results and supporter costs but does not state a numerical baseline cost schedule beyond the next-token track display.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy; supporter costs for Spread are referenced to the token track, whose numeric schedule is not given in summary.

answers.answer: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay. Officers determine the number of Evening military operations. Organize is an Evening operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score uncovered VP; no Supporter, adjacency, or Martial Law cost, but legal placement is required. Losing a base discards all Supporters matching its clearing including birds, removes half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discards excess Supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight Train; Evening Organize.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step does not add refreshes this step. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from forest can move only to adjacent clearing. At Evening, if in forest Rest by returning damaged items to Satchel face up; this does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after forest Rest, then discard to five and check capacity.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening steps.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin when its last item is taken. Quest: choose a face-up quest matching the clearing, exhaust its two listed items, complete it, and choose either VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards; draw a replacement quest. No card pays a quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its current face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except that when attacking alongside an ally, removing more of that ally's warriors as battle hits than items damaged makes the ally Hostile at battle end. During battle on your own turn, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; add normal building/token removal points. No Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that faction has no warriors in the clearing may you instead remove another faction piece. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Relationships: Hostile, Infamy, Aid; Daylight Strike; Attack with ally.

answers.answer: Vagabond coalition is available with four or more players, during own Daylight at 10 or more VP, by activating dominance with another player not already in a coalition. Choose the player with the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond, choosing among ties. Put Vagabond's score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies; if the partner is Hostile, they become Indifferent. Coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
